question: Where can I get the boundaries (geometry) of protected natural areas in the United States, at every designation level (international, national and regional), with category and designation date?

answer.summary: Start with USGS PAD-US 4.1 for US protected-area boundaries. The queried fee layer had 296,456 polygons. Date_Est was filled for about 24% of that layer. USGS separately lists combined web services and a full geodatabase for overlapping designations, easements and marine areas. Protected Planet supplies international and regional designations. Commercial reuse requires permission.
main_caveats: The tested endpoint is the fee layer. For overlaps, use the separate combined services listed by USGS. One area can span several rows, as Yellowstone does.
Date_Est represents the year of the current name and designation where reported. It was filled for about 24% of the fee features. Protected Planet status_yr was 0 for about 52% of US records.
USGS strongly discourages comparing two PAD-US versions to find changes in protection; 4.0 and 4.1 services both stay online, so name the version used.

A category or protected-area record does not prove legal prohibitions: PAD-US also holds military land (MIL), public land and generic 'other' designations, and local park data is incomplete in some states.
WDPA data may not be put to commercial use without UNEP-WCMC permission; the public layer cites October 2026 while the country page cites November 2026.
answer.confidence_reason: Service and WDPA layers queried with counts and an identifiable area; USGS pages and the full geodatabase were blocked to curl and read through WebFetch; state sources other than one form-gated database were not checked.

attributes.note: PAD-US 4.1 service returns polygons (GeoJSON tested for Yellowstone); WDPA polygon layer holds 50,964 US sites. Agency-sourced boundaries, no positional accuracy stated.
PAD-US covers federal, state, local, tribal and private lands; international designations only in WDPA (43 US records) and registries; local data is incomplete in some states.
attributes.gap_note: The endpoint tested exposes the fee layer. USGS separately documents combined services and the full geodatabase. The full download and UNESCO register were not retrieved.

attributes.note: PAD-US Des_Tp (63 codes such as NP, WA, SP, LP), GAP_Sts, IUCN_Cat and Loc_Ds; WDPA desig_eng and iucn_cat. Generic codes (SOTH, LOTH, FOTH) do not state legal limits.
PAD-US Date_Est (a 4-character year) is filled for 71,609 of 296,456 features (24%); WDPA status_yr is 0 for 26,556 of 50,964 US records. Source update dates are separate.
attributes.gap_note: Most features carry no establishment year; USGS says the field is not fully populated and points to agencies for dates; no per-designation date was found for overlapping layers.

local_terms.meaning: Protected Areas Database of the United States, USGS inventory of public and some private protected lands
PAD-US designation type code: NP National Park, WA Wilderness Area, SP State Park, LP Local Park, MIL Military Land
1 to 4 protection level for biodiversity (1 strict, 4 no known mandate)
Fee is ownership of land; an easement protects land owned by someone else
PAD-US Date of Establishment, a four-character year
World Database on Protected Areas run by UNEP-WCMC; site_id is the WDPA code
Wetland of international importance under the Ramsar Convention
Federal designation under the Wilderness Act, coded WA
